patch.value: GH-1775: the secret guard flags bare environment-variable references (api_key: ${API_KEY}) as credentials since the #1704 widening

GH-1775 (filed 2026-11-23 while moving the extension package pm-memory to 2026.11.23; draft unbraind/pm-memory#96 is blocked on it). Since the credential-key guard widened beyond password (pm-gh1704), scanMutationSecrets reports credential_key_assignment for a value made only of a reference under a credential key: scanMutationSecrets(JSON.stringify({ title: 'api_key: ${API_KEY}', updated: '2026-11-23T00:00:00.000Z' })) returns [] on 2026.11.14 and a credential_key_assignment finding on 2026.11.23. A reference names where a secret lives and holds no secret value, so trackers that document configuration (api_key: ${API_KEY}, token=$GITHUB_TOKEN) have their mutations refused. pm-hw00c2 (closed) made CREDENTIAL_VALUE capture a value that holds a run-time reference whole and judge the literal left after expansion; a bare reference leaves no literal, so whether it should still match is the question this item settles. Expected: a value made only of a reference (${NAME}, $NAME, ${{ secrets.NAME }} and similar) is not a credential under any credential key; a reference with an attached literal or a literal value is still flagged. Duplicate check: searched secret guard environment variable reference credential key bare reference; pm-hw00c2, pm-ycgb5g and pm-gh1704 are closed and own the literal-concatenation and key-widening rules.

Bare references under api_key, client_secret, token, secret and password produce no finding in JSON, YAML, dotenv, XML and quoted-key forms; Attached literals and literal values are still flagged; A corpus test pins both sides, with the 2026.11.23 behaviour as the negative control
Reference-only configuration values pass the secret guard while literal credentials stay refused

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Root cause (2026-11-23, reproduced on the 2026.11.23 build and compared with 2026.11.14 in a scratch prefix): the false positive needs a SIBLING member after the string that holds the assignment. With the title alone the scan is clean; with any later member it flags. The flat scan reads the serialized JSON text, and both key-named value grammars (credential_key_assignment and password_assignment) read a quoted piece after a reference as a shell concatenation. So the closing quote of the enclosing JSON string, the comma and the next key's opening quote form a quoted piece whose body is only a comma, and the literal judged after reference expansion becomes comma + next key + colon + next value. A 588-case grid (7 keys x 7 reference spellings x 12 forms) measured 98 false positives on main: braced, defaulted and angle references in compact JSON text, arrays, nested objects and Python-repr text for every key, plus password with a bare dollar-name or command reference in the same forms (wordComplete treats any quote after an unquoted value as a possible concatenation, so the dollar-name stays literal), plus password with a bare Windows percent-name in every form (flagged on 2026.11.14 too; the credential-key rule already treats it as a placeholder). Fix plan: a quoted piece whose body is only JSON structure punctuation is a string boundary, never a concatenated piece, in both grammars; wordComplete treats the same boundary after an unquoted value as the end of its word; a whole-value percent-name is a reference for every key-named rule.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Decision note (2026-11-23): two pins from the pm-hw00c2 review loop (Codex round 10) are reversed on purpose. They kept a CONSTANT_CASE dollar-name literal whenever any quote followed an unquoted password value, even where that quote closes the enclosing string (a JSON array element followed by a sibling, and a JSON member value ending the object), and a cut-reference linear-time input counted one finding for the same reason. GH-1775 requires those JSON forms to be clean. The new rule (closesEnclosingString) ends the word only when the quote is followed by blanks and a line break or the end of the text, or by JSON structure, optional blanks and the next member or element; the Codex round 10 passphrase case (a quote followed by a space and words) still keeps the variable literal and is still reported. The differential over 3,952 cases against the published 2026.11.23 bundle gained no finding; every lost finding is a bare reference, a whole-value percent name, or the residual (19) shape recorded on pm-jcz7qz.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Redesign after Codex review round 1 (2026-11-23, 12 findings, 4 P1). The first approach guessed from local shapes whether a quote closes an enclosing string (a structure run and a next string that closes within 4,096 characters). Codex showed it misreads YAML doubled single quotes, accepts a quote no string opened (a YAML plain scalar ending in a double quote), misses JSON whitespace before a separator, and flips verdicts when the next member is longer than the bound. Replaced by a lexical rule: flatMatches computes the string state before every position in one linear pass per scan (quote opens or closes its own kind, the other kind is data, backslash escapes, line breaks end strings); when a key-named rule's value sits in an open string whose closing quote lies inside or right after the capture and a word end follows that quote (whitespace, end of text, or structure then the next member, element, line break or end), the match is truncated there, wordComplete treats that quote as the end of the word, and the scan resumes at the quote so keys in later members are still scanned. The regex grammar is identical to main again. The whole-value Windows percent-name addition was dropped (it was not a whole-value check, and the issue does not require it; recorded as residual 20 on pm-jcz7qz). Measured after the redesign: grid 0 false positives outside the dropped percent case; differential over 3,952 cases versus 2026.11.23 gains 12 true positives (literals attached to a reference inside a Python-repr string) and loses only bare references, sibling-swallowing cases, and residual 18; scans stay linear (6M characters in 1.7 s, doubling per size step).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 (2026-11-23): a prose apostrophe (customer's) opened a string in the lexical pass, so a quoted password after it read as the closing quote and was dropped; a quote right after a letter, digit or underscore no longer opens a string. The Windows percent-name is now implemented as a whole-value check rather than dropped: unquoted text is whole only when blanks then a line break or the end follow it, or when it ends at the string it sits in; quoted values, decoded literals and element bodies are whole by construction; a dotenv or set line with more words after the reference stays reported. The credential-key reference-free grammar now excludes a percent-name only when it ends the value, so a literal attached to it is reported (main missed it). Grid: 0 false positives over every key, reference (percent-name included) and form. Differential versus 2026.11.23: 126 gained true positives (attached literals after a percent-name or inside a Python-repr string), losses limited to bare references, sibling-swallowing cases and residual 18.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 3 (2026-11-24): fixed a regression where a YAML flow apostrophe (a plain note scalar holding an apostrophe before a password key) made the password's own opening quote read as the enclosing closer; a value is never cut at its own first character, which keeps main's reading there (and keeps the empty-assignment JSON shape flagged as main does). U+2028 and U+2029 no longer end a string in the lexical pass (JSON allows them raw); a closing quote followed by an XML tag end or by structure and an unquoted YAML flow key now ends the word; blanks after the structure are padding however many. Residual recorded: multi-line double-quoted YAML scalars (a raw line feed inside the string) still end the string state at the line feed.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: CodeRabbit review round 1 (2026-11-24, Major): the next-member shortcut cut a shell concatenation written inside a string (echo, a quoted reference, the closing quote, a comma and a quoted literal), which was residual 18. The shortcut now applies only when the enclosing string is a member or element of a container: its opening quote follows a bracket, brace, comma or colon and optional blanks (JSON, YAML flow, Python repr). The lexical pass records each string's opening quote and finds it by binary search, so the scan stays linear. A string a command word or prose opened keeps main's concatenated reading; blanks, line breaks, the end of the text and XML tag ends still end the word for any string. Residual 18 is resolved: the differential no longer loses those shapes.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 4 (2026-11-24): fixed a regression where a stray YAML apostrophe let the apostrophe inside a real double-quoted password cut the value, and the same shape for a quoted default inside a reference: a quote inside the capture that a blank follows can only be data of the value's own quoted text, so it is never a cut point. A JSON member value that starts on the next line is a container member (the look-back skips line breaks). Differential and grid unchanged (0 false positives; 126 gained true positives).

value.text: Hosted CI on b324faa40 (2026-11-24): Coverage shard 2/4 failed the linear-time pin in secret-guard-references-and-members.spec.ts (6.4 s against a 5 s budget under coverage instrumentation), because the first lexical design materialised a Uint8Array of string states for the whole 16M-character input and rescanned whole captures. Replaced by a forward-only lexer per flat scan, advanced only to each judged value's start (value starts strictly increase across a scan) and through a value only while a string is open there, with the open string's opener tracked on the lexer instead of an array. Behaviour is identical (same 3,952-case differential, grid and every review reproduction), the pinned test drops to about 0.3 s locally, and both changed source files are 100 percent covered by the targeted suites.

patch.value: A value made only of a reference is clean under every credential key in JSON, YAML, dotenv, XML and quoted-key forms, while literal values and attached literals are still reported

The two key-named secret rules now end a value at the closing quote of the string it sits in, found by a forward-only lexical pass per scan, when a word end follows that quote (whitespace, the end, structure then a line break, or structure then the next member for container strings, or a tag end for attribute values), so the next JSON member is never read as a quoted piece concatenated to a reference. A value is never cut at its own first character or at a quote inside its own quoted text, shell and prose strings keep their concatenated reading, and the regex grammar is identical to main. A whole-value Windows percent-name is a line-complete placeholder for every key-named rule, and the credential-key placeholder exclusion applies only when the percent-name ends the value. Measured: the 588-case grid went from 98 false positives on 2026.11.23 to 0; a 3,952-case differential gains 126 true positives (attached literals after a percent-name or inside a Python repr) and loses only bare references and next-member-swallowing cases. Review: Codex rounds 1 to 5, Greptile rounds 1 to 4 and CodeRabbit round 1 addressed; residuals recorded on pm-jcz7qz.
The issue reproduction and every grid case are clean, the negative-control half stays reported, and scans stay linear (the 16M-character pin runs in about 0.3 s)
Bare run-time references are no longer judged as credentials in serialized JSON text or any other form; literal and attached-literal credentials stay reported
